decisions.title: Datastore for the payments ledger
decisions.headline: 1 critical assumption behind ADR-007 no longer holds.

broken.statement: Write volume will stay within the projected ~1,800 writes/second that a single well‑tuned Postgres primary can sustain
broken.explanation: Peak ledger writes reached 3,140 writes/sec in Dec 2025 and FP&A projects 4,500 writes/sec for next year, far exceeding the 1,800 writes/sec limit the decision relied on.

broken.statement: Finance month‑end reporting can continue on the same database with only minor query rewrites
broken.explanation: Finance month‑end reporting has been migrated to Snowflake and direct queries against the production ledger are now disabled, invalidating the assumption that reporting can continue on the same PostgreSQL instance.

decisions.title: Infrastructure as code with Terraform
decisions.headline: ADR-009 still applies: no recorded change contradicts its assumptions.

decisions.title: Caching strategy for the rate-quote API
decisions.headline: 1 critical assumption behind ADR-012 no longer holds; PM-2025-02 records this approach failing.

broken.statement: All shippers are located in the United States and Canada (North America)
broken.explanation: The original assumption that all shippers are in North America is invalidated by the EU launch, which added shippers in Germany, the Netherlands, and Poland.

decisions.title: Event backbone for shipment tracking events
decisions.headline: 1 critical assumption behind ADR-015 no longer holds.

broken.statement: The platform team has sufficient Kafka operational expertise to manage MSK.
broken.explanation: Platform team expertise has degraded: Jin Park left the team and only Marcus remains with Kafka experience, and a post‑mortem shows the team’s Kafka knowledge now rests on a single person and the runbook lacked coverage for the failure mode.

decisions.title: Synchronous REST between booking and pricing
decisions.headline: ADR-019 still applies: no recorded change contradicts its assumptions.

decisions.title: Identity provider for shipper and staff logins
decisions.headline: 1 critical assumption behind ADR-021 no longer holds.

broken.statement: No current customer contracts require SOC 2 attestation, so compliance‑grade audit logging is not mandatory now
broken.explanation: Enterprise prospects now require SOC 2 Type II attestation, making the original “no SOC 2 required” assumption false.

decisions.title: Monorepo for web frontends
decisions.headline: ADR-024 still applies: no recorded change contradicts its assumptions.

decisions.title: Retry policy for carrier API calls
decisions.headline: ADR-027 still applies: no recorded change contradicts its assumptions.

decisions.title: Invoice generation as a nightly batch
decisions.headline: ADR-031 still applies, but 2 supporting conditions changed.

broken.statement: A nightly batch can finish within the 01:00–04:00 UTC maintenance window
broken.explanation: Signal [SIG-2026-05] reports the nightly invoice batch now runs 5 hours 40 minutes, exceeding the 01:00–04:00 UTC maintenance window.

broken.statement: The nightly invoice volume (~120,000) is within the capacity of a batch process
broken.explanation: The same signal [SIG-2026-05] notes the invoice volume has grown to ~340,000, causing the batch to overrun the window, indicating the volume exceeds the batch’s capacity.

decisions.title: Managed feature-flag service
decisions.headline: ADR-034 still applies: no recorded change contradicts its assumptions.
